text:
Mitch Marner's first fall in Vegas has gone the way his whole career has gone: the puck finds him, and then it finds somebody else. He has 21 assists and three goals in 19 games, 15 points in his last ten, and the power-play play everyone saw against Utah (drive the slot, fake the shot, slide it to Jack Eichel) is the Golden Knights' new signature.

The goals are the odd part. Three on 5.3 expected, shooting under 7%, when his usual range sits closer to 13%. He keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances, so we'd treat this as a dry spell, not a change in who he is. His on-ice numbers carry no luck at all, which makes the 24 points look solid.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.9 wins last season, 16th among forwards, almost all of it from even-strength offense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the part that rarely makes highlights: 62% of his zone exits leave with possession. The Toronto chapter still gets written about plenty. In Vegas he has simply been the setup man they paid for.
